Venaani calls for emergency FMD relief f.final_text: The Ministry of Finance acknowledges the concerns raised regarding the financial pressures faced by farmers and businesses during the current Foot-and-Mouth Disease (FMD) situation. We understand the urgency expressed by stakeholders, including calls for temporary relief from certain financial obligations to support economic stability in affected regions. It is important to clarify that tax administration and revenue collection are the responsibility of the Namibia Revenue Agency (Namra), which operates independently while adhering to national fiscal policies. However, the Ministry remains committed to supporting the broader economic welfare of Namibians. Relevant authorities are currently reviewing the specific circumstances to determine appropriate measures that balance fiscal responsibility with the need for targeted support. We are working closely with partner institutions to assess viable options for relief. The government remains dedicated to safeguarding the livelihoods of our citizens and will continue to engage constructively with all stakeholders to ensure a fair and sustainable resolution to these challenges.

Woman arrested for drugs worth N$2.2m at.final_text: The Ministry of Home Affairs, Immigration, Safety and Security notes the media reports regarding the recent arrest of an individual at Goreagab, Windhoek, for the possession of prohibited dependency-producing substances. The Ministry confirms that the Namibian Police Force has taken the suspect into custody, and she is currently facing charges under the Abuse of Dependency-Producing Substances and Rehabilitation Centres Act, as well as the Prevention of Organised Crime Act. This action underscores the Ministry’s unwavering commitment to enforcing the rule of law and combating the illicit drug trade, which poses a significant threat to public safety and social stability. The relevant authorities are proceeding with the necessary legal processes to ensure that justice is served in accordance with the Namibian Constitution. The Ministry reassures the public that sustained efforts will be made to disrupt criminal networks and safeguard our communities. We call on citizens to remain vigilant and to cooperate fully with law enforcement in reporting suspicious activities.

Keetmanshoop man arrested for killing gi.ministry: Ministry of Home Affairs, Immigration, Safety and Security
Keetmanshoop man arrested for killing gi.final_text: The Ministry of Home Affairs, Immigration, Safety and Security acknowledges media reports regarding the arrest of a suspect in Keetmanshoop for the killing of his girlfriend. The Ministry confirms that the suspect has been taken into custody and that the next of kin have been duly informed. It is noted that the victim was transported to Rundu Intermediate Hospital, where she remains in serious condition. The Namibian Police Force is actively conducting a thorough investigation to establish the full circumstances of the incident. This case is being handled in strict accordance with the law and established police protocols. The Ministry reaffirms its commitment to public safety and justice, assuring the public that all relevant authorities are cooperating to ensure the matter is resolved appropriately. The Ministry urges the public to continue cooperating with law enforcement and to report any concerns through official channels.

Will Amutse pay for cement merger error?.final_text: The Ministry of Home Affairs, Immigration, Safety and Security notes the recent parliamentary queries regarding the merger of Cheetah Cement and Ohorongo Cement. The Ministry wishes to clarify that decisions concerning industrial mergers fall under the jurisdiction of the Ministry of Industries, Mines and Energy, and are subject to review by the Namibian Competition Commission. The Ministry of Home Affairs is not the regulatory body responsible for approving or overturning such commercial transactions, nor does it manage the operational decisions of other ministries. The Namibian government maintains a robust system of checks and balances where all administrative actions are conducted in accordance with the Constitution and relevant legislation. Any concerns regarding the procedural integrity of such decisions are being addressed by the relevant authorities through established legal and administrative channels. The Ministry reassures the public that all government entities operate within the rule of law, and that taxpayer funds are managed with strict adherence to fiscal responsibility and accountability standards.
